title: Sundial curiosity
text:
Title: Sundial curiosity

A somewhat notable effect, owing its origin to the equation of time, is seen in the times of sunrise and sunset given in 
our almanacs. On November 8, for example, the sun rises at Greenwich at 6h. 58m., and sets at 4h. 31m., thus 
apparently making the afternoon about half an hour longer than the morning. As reckoned by the sun-dial, however, the
morning and afternoon would differ only by a few seconds, and the peculiarity noted arises simply from the fact that 
our clocks keep time with the mean, and not with the true sun.
